newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX Q1 solid vs strong yr-ago comparisons.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX Q1 solid vs strong yr-ago comparisons.

text.p: NYNEX Corp reported first quarter earnings a few cents ahead of expectations, excluding the effects of an enhanced pension offer, and in spite of difficult comparisons to a strong year-ago first quarter.
The company said its total adjusted telecommunications revenues were $3.38 billion, up 1.4 percent over the $3.32 billion in the first quarter of 1996.

NYNEX said a sales "blitz" helped increase revenues for new value-added services like Caller ID, Call Waiting and voice messaging by 35.1 percent and drove up total non-usage revenues 6.0 percent, the strongest gains in over two years.

First quarter adjusted operating earnings of $0.92 per share compared to the $0.90 per share First Call consensus estimate for the quarter and the $0.83 per share reported in the prior year first quarter.

The latest quarter's results exclude a $0.56 per share charge to cover an enhanced pension offer to 2,900 employees, while the 1996 first quarter excluded a charge of $0.16 per share for about 960 employees who accepted the offer.
Montgomery analyst Bill Vogel said the NYNEX results were "outstanding," given difficult comparsions versus a year ago, and believes they may accelerate during the remainder of 1997.

"I am confident that the company is going to deliver solid double-digit growth in (earnings per share) for the forseeable future," Vogel said, adding that, "A strong case can be built for accelerating momentum into the balance of the year."

The company said underlying growth in subscription revenues from value-added services in addition to basic access, was partially offset by a 3.3 percent decline in usage revenues over the first quarter of last year.
1996 first quarter results were aided by sky-rocketing residential call volumes during a series of winter storms.
NYNEX said robust sales of business services continued in the face of competition, with Centrex sales rising 12.9 percent and private line revenues increasing 13.1 percent.
It said revenues from Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) lines grew 93 percent over the first quarter of 1996 as the number of ISDN lines in service rose to more than 136,000.
The company said access minutes of use rose 5.9 percent, year-over-year. NYNEX said it has now signed up more than three million high-value customers for its new calling plans.
Worldwide, NYNEX access lines, including the share of its unconsolidated ventures, grew 4.7 percent versus a year-ago.
Consolidated revenues increased 1.9 percent over the first quarter of 1996 to $3.4 billion.

The company said its jointly owned wireless business, Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile (BANM), revenues of which are not consolidated, grew 22.8 percent. Including NYNEX's share of revenues from BANM and its other unconsolidated businesses, total corporate revenues grew 3.7 percent, it said.

NYNEX said its operating margin grew 1.7 percentage points over the first quarter of 1996, to 23.1 percent, and operating income grew 10.1 percent, to $781.8 million. NYNEX operating margin has expanded nearly five percentage points since the beginning of 1994.
The number of lines in service in its northeastern United States business rose 3.5 percent to 17.9 million. At NYNEX's overseas operations, access lines increased 51.4 percent.

Worldwide wireless operations sustained their rapid growth. BANM's customer gains set a first-quarter record, as net additions of 224,000 increased the total number of subscribers to 4.6 million, a 29.6 percent increase over the first quarter of 1996.
In information services, NYNEX Information Resources Company (NIRC) increased the total number of advertisers 7.4 percent over the first quarter of last year.

"NYNEX sustained the momentum it has built over the past two years and delivered double-digit net income growth for the eighth straight quarter," NYNEX Chairman and Chief Executive Ivan Seidenberg said in a statement.
Montgomery analyst Vogel agreed, saying that, "This momentum bodes extremely well for the second quarter."
NYNEX is awaiting approval from U.S. regulators to go ahead with its proposed merger with Bell Atlantic Corp.
NYNEX shares were up 1/2 point at 44-1/2 in early morning trading Wednesday on light volume.
((-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736 ))
